subject: pathology
title: Chronic and granulomatous inflammation

steps.tx: Chronic inflammation is a prolonged response in which injury and repair occur together. **Chronic inflammation** lasts weeks to months, and **macrophages and lymphocytes** dominate the tissue infiltrate rather than neutrophils. It follows unresolved acute inflammation, persistent infection, toxic exposure or autoimmunity, and fibrosis often replaces tissue that has been lost.
steps.say: Chronic inflammation is prolonged and injury with repair occurs together in tissues. The infiltrate is dominated by macrophages, lymphocytes and plasma cells over months. Persistent infection and autoimmunity are common causes of this pattern of inflammation. Fibrosis develops frequently because lost tissue is replaced by scar.

steps.tx: The macrophage is the central cell that drives chronic inflammation and repair. **Classical activation** by interferon gamma enhances microbial killing, and **alternative activation** by interleukin 4 and interleukin 13 promotes healing. Classically activated cells also damage tissue, whereas alternatively activated cells produce growth factors that promote angiogenesis and fibrosis.
steps.say: The macrophage is central because it controls killing, clearance and repair processes. Classical activation is induced by interferon gamma and microbial products in tissue. Alternative activation is induced by interleukin 4 and interleukin 13 in healing tissue. The balance is important because it determines destruction versus repair.

left.title: Classical activation (M1)
points: Induced by interferon gamma and microbial products
Produces nitric oxide and reactive oxygen species

steps.tx: A granuloma is an organised collection of activated macrophages that walls off persistent agents. A **granuloma** contains epithelioid macrophages and multinucleate giant cells, and **Langhans giant cells** arrange nuclei at the cell periphery. Foreign body giant cells scatter nuclei randomly, and mycobacteria and fungi are classic agents that provoke granulomas.
steps.say: A granuloma is organised because epithelioid macrophages cluster with surrounding lymphocytes tightly. Giant cells form when macrophages fuse during persistent stimulation in tissue. Nuclear arrangement is peripheral in Langhans cells whereas nuclei are scattered in others. Mycobacteria provoke granulomas because they resist intracellular killing strongly.

rows: May contain inclusions such as Schaumann bodies

steps.tx: Tuberculous and sarcoid granulomas differ mainly by the presence of central necrosis. **Caseous necrosis** gives tuberculosis a cheese like centre, and **sarcoidosis** produces tight non caseating granulomas in lungs and hilar nodes. Histology alone rarely proves the cause, so special stains, culture and molecular tests are essential for confirmation.
steps.say: Caseous necrosis is present in tuberculosis and it gives a cheese like appearance. Sarcoid granulomas are non caseating and they involve lungs and hilar nodes commonly. Angiotensin converting enzyme is raised in many patients with sarcoidosis clinically. Confirmation is required because histology alone rarely proves causation.

vis.alt: Concentric architecture of a caseating tuberculous granuloma: central acellular eosinophilic caseous necrosis, surrounded by epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated horseshoe Langhans giant cells, enclosed by a rim of CD4 T lymphocytes and outer fibroblasts.
vis.caption: Caseating granuloma: central necrosis, horseshoe Langhans giant cells, epithelioid macrophages, and peripheral lymphocytic cuff.

steps.tx: Repair by fibrosis occurs when tissue loss is large or injury persists. **Granulation tissue** contains plump fibroblasts and new capillaries, and **transforming growth factor beta** stimulates fibroblasts to deposit collagen. New vessels form by angiogenesis during healing, and granulation tissue must not be confused with a granuloma despite similar names.
steps.say: Fibrosis develops when tissue loss is substantial or injury persists chronically. Fibroblasts deposit collagen because transforming growth factor beta stimulates them strongly. Granulation tissue is vascular and it contains plump fibroblasts with loose matrix. The name is confusing because granulation tissue differs from granulomas.

steps.tx: This illustration shows granulation tissue with macrophages, fibroblasts and new vessels. **Granulation tissue** contains plump fibroblasts and **collagen deposition**, and new capillaries form by angiogenesis in loose matrix. The title stresses that this repair tissue is not a granuloma, which is a classic trap in pathology examinations.
steps.say: This image shows macrophages, plump fibroblasts and new capillaries in healing tissue. Collagen fibres are deposited as repair progresses through the injured area progressively. Angiogenesis is active because new vessels supply the developing repair tissue. Granulation tissue is shown because it differs from a granuloma.
